text:
infra-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool us-west-2 (pool-42) p99 latency > 6s for streaming; SLO breach triggered. Auto-escalation: paging #incidents and on-call.

sarah-eng: seeing p95 jump ~1.2s -> 2.8s, p99 at 6.3s, streaming stalls reported by customers. Queue depth spiked to 900/1000.

mike-oncall: oncall here, ack. I'm pulling metrics. what's current free GPU count?

jane-sre: free GPUs 0, warm pools 0, all 8 nodes at 100% utilization. Autoscaler shows pending scale-up but warmup handshake failing: "handshake timeout" in logs.

ops-runner: attaching relevant logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:02:12Z pool-42 autoscaler: request_scale +4
2026-03-15T15:02:18Z pool-42 warmup: slot-alloc handshake timeout after 5s
2026-03-15T15:02:30Z queue: depth=912 inflight=880 avg_latency=3.8
2026-03-15T15:02:35Z streaming: tailstall detected seq=0x7f timeout
```

sam-support: multiple customers (tenant ids: t-881, t-992) reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. One customer error: "stream aborted (partial)." Escalating to AMs.

lia-sd: can we temporarily route small requests to smaller model variant (redwood-small) while warmup finishes?

sarah-eng: good idea. Model-routing policy allows fallback to compatible variant. But streaming for long-context callers will be affected.

mike-oncall: mitigation plan:
1) throttle tenant t-881 burst by 50% via quota override.
2) enable fallback routing to redwood-small for non-chat endpoints.
3) bump pool-42 desired by +2 manually and force warmup.
4) evict >30s long-running requests from queue if possible.

jane-sre: executing step 3 now: `infractl pool scale --pool pool-42 --add 2 --force-warmup`

infra-bot: action accepted: scaled +2 requested. Warmup tasks scheduled.

ops-runner: implementing eviction: `queuectl evict --pool pool-42 --age >30s --dry-run` shows 48 candidates. Executing.

sam-support: contacting tenants: sent initial message to t-881 and t-992 support contacts. Noting degraded streaming and possible partial outputs. Asking to pause heavy realtime workloads.

sarah-eng: adding cache hints: enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts from t-992 to reduce compute.

lia-sd: routing update complete for non-chat endpoints -> redwood-small. Note: chat streaming still on heavy model.

mike-oncall: throttle applied to t-881: 50% burst limit. Confirm?

sam-support: confirmed from tenant side they see reduced error rate after throttle. Good.

jane-sre: warmup succeeded for +1 node; second node failing handshake with `certificate not yet valid` on warmup agent.

sarah-eng: that cert z-index is odd. Possibly clock skew on new nodes. Checking NTP.

ops-runner: NTP drift found (~120s) on node i-0a3bc; restarting timesync.

infra-bot: timesync restart succeeded on i-0a3bc, warmup handshake retried and succeeded.

jane-sre: all new nodes warmed up. Pool capacity increased. Queue depth down to 210, p99 trending to 1.9s.

sarah-eng: streaming stalls count dropped 87% in last 5m. Still seeing tail at ~2.2s for long contexts.

mike-oncall: customer impact: t-881 saw ~20% requests partial, now down to 3%. t-992 partials down from 15% -> 2%. Notified AMs.

sam-support: AMs acknowledged, prepping post-incident customer note.

lia-sd: recommended postmortem actions:
- improve autoscaler handshake retries and exponential backoff
- add NTP health check to warmup flow
- add tenant-level burst protection by default for newly onboarded heavy tenants
- create runbook steps for forcible fallback routing

sarah-eng: agree. Also add metric alert for queue depth > 600 triggering pre-scale check.

mike-oncall: current status: mitigations deployed, pool stable, p99 under SLO at 95% confidence but continue monitoring for 30m. I'll remain on this thread.

sam-support: keeping customers updated every 15m.

jane-sre: creating incident ticket and assigning owners for follow-ups.

infra-bot: incident recorded: INC-20260315-0425. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-20260315-0425

sarah-eng: thanks everyone. tagging for follow-up: @jane-sre (autoscaler fixes), @lia-sd (tenant throttling defaults), @sarah-eng (metrics/alerts), @sam-support (customer comms).

mike-oncall: closing live mitigation. Monitoring window started.
